HotLoop screens are P&IDs. A CODESYS PLC's own alarms show in HotLoop's alarm list and an acknowledge goes back to the PLC, a script run always ends, a box's data volume always reads, and the UniFi Protect, Access and power roadmap lines are shipped. Built for amd64 only; the multi-arch build follows as the next version.

## What changed

- **Screens are P&IDs.** Drop tanks, pumps, valves, heat exchangers, filters, instruments and junctions on a symbol page, then drag from one connection point to another: the pipe lays itself in right angles around everything on the page, tees off with a junction where you drop it on another pipe, and re-routes while you move a symbol. Every pipe carries its medium (water, steam, fuel, air, power, signal and more, each with a color, a code and a line pattern, so color is never the only carrier) and moves with its tag or a rule. Every symbol page gets a toolbar to zoom, pan, show a mini-map and switch to the gray high performance view, and a P&ID saves, exports and imports in the same screen file. See [Dashboards](/iot/dashboards/) and [Screen files](/iot/screen-file/).
- **A CODESYS PLC's own alarms show in HotLoop's alarm list.** A project's Alarm Configuration keeps alarm groups and classes, and alarms that watch a variable. A CODESYS device now reads the ones its PLC's alarm manager holds (active, waiting to be acknowledged, acknowledged while the condition still holds), and an acknowledge made in HotLoop goes back to the PLC. A PLC with none to give is left alone. It needs the HotLoop Alarms library and one block in the project. See CODESYS-ALARMS.md.
- **The box's data volume always reads.** A box with nothing mounted under `/data` has no `/data`, and the box-health `data_util_pct` tag read bad with "no such file or directory". It now reads the volume the data folder will be made on. See [Protocols and drivers](/iot/protocols/#box-health).
- **A script run always ends.** When the database refused the write of a script run's end, HotLoop logged it and gave up, so the run read "running" for the life of the process with its slot long since free. The write is now asked again, up to five times with a short wait between.
- **UniFi Protect, Access and SmartPower PDU outlets are shipped on the roadmap.** They arrived as devices in 4.23.6, built to the published APIs, with Protect's every path matching the 7.4.102 document. See [HotLoop roadmap](/roadmap/).
- **A TwinCAT screen is proven in a browser.** The TwinCAT PackML example is imported with its frames, rendered, and a lamp follows a live register.
- **Tests wait for what they are waiting for.** The panel throttle wait is checked as arithmetic, the forSec hold's timer is in the test's hands and not raced against a sleep, the Apache Kafka topic test deletes its topics at once and has the time a slow box needs, and an API test no longer bounds a sign-in by one sample, because a loaded box answers four times slower than it did a second before.

## Migrations

None.

## API changes

None. No route changed. A symbol page's configuration takes `pipes`, `view` and a symbol's `rot`, and a saved screen file carries them.

## Upgrading from 4.23.6

A plain `helm upgrade`. No migration and no new secret. A symbol page with no pipes is drawn as before.

## What is not proven

- The PLC alarm path ran against a real CODESYS Control for Linux SL 4.22.0.0 runtime with the alarm lab program.
- Protect, Access and the PDU's outlets follow the published APIs, and the bench run on real gear follows at the office.
